changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 6 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/8653-listview-title-retired-rowactiondefs-pinned.md`

- names `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `title` — **retired.** `ListView` resolved its export filename through `schema.label || (schema as any).title`. `@objectstack/spec/ui`'s `ListViewSchema` refuses `title` **by name** (`unrecognized_keys: ['title']`) while `ObjectGridPropsSchema` **accepts** it; `packages/types` mirrors the platform contract rather than ruling over it, so declaring `title` on `ListViewSchema` would have made this repo accept what the platform save gate rejects. That asymmetry is also why objectui#6639 could take the *declare* branch for `ObjectGridSchema.title` one package over and this site could not. A parse-based census of `apps/ examples/ content/` and `packages/` found **zero** `list-view` nodes authoring `title`, so the retirement costs no author a filename. Over that same corpus the instrument reports **three** `object-grid` nodes carrying the key: **two authored** ones, both in `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`, plus one that is not authored at all — `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` composes `title: schema.table?.title` onto a grid node it builds, so it is a producer writing the key rather than an author declaring it. `ObjectGrid`'s own `title` reads are untouched — they remain declared, ruled and read.

### `.changeset/object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.md`

- names `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **What was measured.** Every reading was taken on the `object-view` node renderer (`packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`, registered by `plugin-view/src/index.tsx`) with `schema.objectName` / `schema.layout` as the positive controls of the same `schema.KEY` query, so each zero is a reading; the repo-wide census of `viewTabBar` finds the key in no source file outside `@object-ui/types` (two doc tables listed it as authorable and are corrected here). The spec side was read through the installed pin (`@objectstack/spec@17.2.0`, `ui` entry, 117 exported object schemas walked; control keys `objectName` / `columns` / `navigation` / `listViews` hit): the three spec-modelled keys are optional slots on `ListViewSchema` and `ObjectListViewSchema`; the six local keys have no spec slot anywhere.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `733fd5ac6` (merge-base with origin/main): 5 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1669 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2263 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36398248213)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `56ad7e877433e6691472e052983d2ec5981283f7`

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Member parity with the delegation.** Measured against `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 (`ComponentPropsMap['object-grid']` and `ObjectListViewSchema`) and head `ObjectGrid.tsx`.
   - The fence reads 31 members off the named view, and `filter` / `sort` are read upstream.
   - Route 2 now reads 16: `columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `grouping`, `rowColor`, the 10 new rungs, and `hiddenFields` applied to the projection.
   - The delegation reads 17 members that route 2 does not:
     - **Ten bucket-① chrome members:** `description`, `emptyState`, `filterableFields`, `sharing`, `addRecord`, `userFilters`, `showRecordCount`, `allowPrinting`, `aria`, `compactToolbar`. None is declared on the spec's `object-grid`, and `ObjectGrid` reads none of them (0 hits each). The exclusion is right.
     - **`inlineEdit`:** not declared on `object-grid`, which has `editable`, and 0 grid reads. The exclusion is right for this rung.
     - **`navigation`:** declared on both and read by `ObjectGrid`'s `useNavigationOverlay`. That hook obeys the `onRowClick` it is handed first (`if (onRowClick) { onRowClick(…); return; }`), and route 2 always passes `handleRowClick`. The exclusion is right for this rung.
     - **Outside bucket ①:** `fieldOrder`, `appearance` and `userActions` are not declared on `object-grid`. **`label` and `data` are declared on both, and `ObjectGrid` reads each**: `schema.label` for the caption and export filename, and `getDataConfig`, which calls `resolveRecordSourceConfig(schema, 'view-data')`.
   - The dev's Acceptance notes and open question name `label` and `fieldOrder` but **omit `data`**. `data` is not read off the named view anywhere outside the fence, on any view type.
2. **Precedence is correct.**
   - `pagination` and `selection` read the named view, then `table.*`. The other eight read the named view only.
   - There is no `activeView` rung, matching this branch's existing `grouping` / `rowColor`, and no new node read.
   - THE FIX row pins the named value beating `table`. The CONTROL row pins the unchanged `table` fallback, and that the other eight take nothing from `table`.
   - Keys that are now `undefined` are harmless. `ObjectGrid` has no key-presence read of these, and `showRowHeightToggle` tests `!== undefined`.
3. **`hiddenFields` follows the protocol's composition.**
   - Spec main `view.zod.ts` (#15184 ruling B) says `hiddenFields` "subtracts from that projection", and that an empty `columns` "declares no projection". `ListView`'s `effectiveFields` makes the same subtraction, and the fence already relays it.
   - Edge cases:
     - A hidden name the view does not project is a no-op, which is the spec's "subtracts nothing". It is unpinned but trivially true.
     - With no projection, `undefined` passes through (pinned, green on base as the control).
     - When every projected field is hidden, `[]` is kept. That is `ListView`'s case 2 (pinned).
     - `fieldOrder`: route 2 carries none, so the two do not interact.
   - Non-blocking divergence: the helper keeps a column entry with no identity. `ListView` drops such an entry when `hiddenFields` is non-empty (`fieldName != null && …`). The input is off-protocol, but the docblock's "the way `ListView` makes it" overstates the match.
4. **`exportOptions` lift is the spec's own.**
   - Spec 17.4.0 `ListViewShape.exportOptions` says: "A bare format array is the legacy spelling and lifts to `{ formats: [...] }` at parse". The pin asserts that parse directly. `ListView.resolvedExportOptions` makes the same lift.
   - It applies only on the named-view path. Route 2 had no node `exportOptions` read before and has none now.
5. **The casts cover only a declared-type gap.**
   - `SpecConditionalFormattingRule.condition` is typed `string`. The spec's rule `condition` is `ExpressionInputSchema`. `ObjectGrid` passes it to `resolveConditionalFormatting`, whose `ruleToPredicate` returns a `FieldRulePredicate` (`string | { dialect?, source }`).
   - `BulkActionDef.visible` is `string | { dialect?, source }`.
   - These are the same values the delegation already hands `ObjectGrid` through `ListView`, so nothing new reaches runtime.
   - The dev's second out-of-scope note is imprecise. The spec's `object-grid` declares `conditionalFormatting: z.unknown()` and `bulkActionDefs: z.array(z.unknown())`, so the gap is against the named view's wire, not against `object-grid`.
   - It deserves a backlog carrier, not "none": a type-only widening of `condition` to `FieldRulePredicate`, which is a Clause-② type move. Not blocking.
6. **The fence is byte-identical.** Extracted from the `#region` line through the `#endregion` line: 186 lines, sha1 `40bc22920811a42b0284f478746ff5a5f6b18d10` on both base and head, and `diff` is empty.
7. **The census has not moved.**
   - `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779` derives the whole-file named-view read set by key. Route 2 adds only keys already read inside the fence, so the count stays 43 read / 21 unread of 64, with bucket ① empty.
   - `readSites` is asserted only for `label` (2) and `name` (1), and both are untouched.
   - Neither 7923 nor 7928 has route-2 prose. No row distinguishes routes, and none should change.
8. **Pins are sound, judged by reading.**
   - Red on base by construction: 8 rows, namely THE FIX, the lift, 4 `hiddenFields` rows and the 2 ViewPreview rows. The 7 green on base are 3 static spec-derivation rows, the node control, the no-projection control and 2 ViewPreview controls. That matches the dev's quoted `8 failed | 7 passed (15)`, then `15 passed`.
   - The ViewPreview pin mounts the real `ViewPreview`, `SchemaRenderer`, registered `object-view` and `ObjectGrid` (not mocked), and reads the DOM.
   - Ablation: leg A plus leg B turn exactly the 8 new rows red out of 797.
   - `695a6ce635..56ad7e8774` is verified to be a 2-line header-comment change.
9. **Docs and changeset contain a false sentence.**
   - Changeset paragraph 3 says route 2 "now reads … each member the protocol declares under the same name on both a named view and `object-grid`, and that `ObjectGrid` reads: [ten]".
   - The README and mdx paragraphs make the same claim: "The grid members the protocol declares under the same name on a named view and on `object-grid` — [ten] — come from the active named view first".
   - Both present the ten as the whole set. `label`, `data` and `navigation` meet the same test and are not read off the named view on route 2. The changeset is frozen once released, which is the class of error member 3 of this card exists to fix.
   - Every other sentence checks out against the code: "nothing else" on base, the `table` fallbacks, "only a declared projection", "delegation unchanged" and `Clause-②`.
10. **Open question: I recommend A, widened by `data`.** Member 4 would be `fieldOrder`, `label`, `data`, `navigation` and `inlineEdit`, dispatched after member 3.
    - **Real need.** `ViewPreview` spreads the whole stored body into the named view. The card records that the console persists `inlineEdit` per view. `fieldOrder` is the spec's declared third composition step. `label` feeds the grid caption and export filename, and `data` feeds the grid's fetch source. I did not measure stored-view usage of `data`.
    - **Long-term fit, measured.** `navigation` is currently inert on both routes. `navigationConfig = schema.navigation` reads only the node, and its `handleRowClick` is the `onRowClick` that both `ObjectGrid` and `ListView`'s `useNavigationOverlay` obey first. One named-first read, outside the fence, fixes both routes. The fence stays byte-identical and the census stays unmoved.
    - **AI-error resistance.** `ObjectGrid` gates `editable` itself: `inlineEditable = (schema.editable ?? false) && objectInlineEditable`. Handing it the named `inlineEdit` cannot widen editing past a grant, so neither member needs a ruling, only pins. B, ruling them out for route 2, would leave keys that parse and are then dropped, which is the declared-not-enforced trap. The spec gives no per-route lever to rule a member out on one route.
